items.prompt: Your last week. What is it for?
items.clock: Month twelve · Monday · town hall Thursday
items.risk: A town hall that still needs its architect.
timeout: Maya spends the week fixing things herself.

hints.text: What would prove the year worked — before you go?

options.label: Write one last complete document of everything you know
options.result: Three hundred pages, finished at 2 a.m. Wednesday. Nobody reads it.
options.consequence: Knowledge written in a hurry is not knowledge held.

options.label: Nothing new: the team runs everything this week — including the town-hall rehearsal — while you only watch and answer what they bring you; anything that still carries only your name gets an owner
options.result: Monday's rehearsal: Noor runs it, Pim runs the failover drill, Galen runs the change freeze. Maya writes down two things that still have only her name.
options.consequence: A last week spent being unnecessary.

options.label: Fix the last three things yourself, properly
options.result: Three things fixed that nobody else has ever touched.
options.consequence: Adds your name to three more things.

options.label: Ask to extend your contract a month, to be safe
options.result: Rashida: “And next month you'll want another.”
options.consequence: Safety that never ends is dependence.

items.title: Over the ocean.
items.body: Maya checks the flight: it leaves Wednesday at 23:00 and lands Thursday late afternoon — twelve hours, most of them over water. The town hall starts at 14:00 headquarters time, when she'll be well out over the ocean. The airline's messaging works above 10,000 feet; on her last trip a message took about five minutes to arrive and a reply another five. Any question to Maya on Thursday costs ten minutes before an answer — longer than the stream can stay dark. Whatever answers first has to be what she built.
items.label: Test: the round trip — and how much of the flight the town hall fills.

items.prompt: Wednesday. The CEO asks Maya to delay her flight and run the town hall herself — ‘just this once’. What do you say?
items.risk: A town hall that never tests what the year built.
timeout: The CEO books Maya a later flight himself.

hints.text: What would staying prove — and what would it cost?

items.note: Draft decision (DR-S12E10). Option B needs Authority & access at LIMITED or better.

options.label: Delay the flight and run it
options.result: It goes perfectly. Nobody learns whether it would have without her.

options.label: Decline, with respect: the team has run harder things without her — the failover in month five, the rotation in month nine — the rota is Rashida's to set; Maya will be reachable by satellite only as a last resort
options.result: The CEO looks at Rashida. Rashida: “She's right. And it's my rota.” The CEO nods.
options.consequence: Trust the architecture, through its owner.

options.label: Agree to dial in from the airport lounge until boarding
options.result: The rehearsal pauses every time Maya's face appears on screen.
options.consequence: The best you can do without the standing to say no — present, and in the way.

options.label: Tell the CEO the team isn't ready
options.result: It is. And now the CEO doesn't think so.

items.title: The architect's models
items.body: When Antoni Gaudí died in 1926, his basilica in Barcelona, the Sagrada Família, was nowhere near finished. He had spent his last years making detailed plaster models and drawings, knowing he wouldn't see it done. In 1936, during the Spanish Civil War, his workshop was burned and many models smashed; builders pieced the fragments back together. A century later, the work still goes on — from what he left behind.

items.alt: An airliner cabin at night, oval windows dark with a few stars; Maya in her seat behind a row of seat backs, looking at the seat-back screen's flight map.
narration: Thursday, 13:30 at headquarters. Somewhere over the ocean, Maya watches a little aeroplane crawl across a map. Everything below this line happens without her — unless she chooses otherwise.
items.caption: Out of reach.

items.title: ‘messages may take several minutes’
items.body: The card in the seat pocket: ‘Messaging available above 10,000 feet. Messages may take several minutes to send and receive.’ Maya had tested it on the way out: five minutes each way, give or take.

items.label: **Sort it:** held by the year — or by Maya?

items.alt: The headquarters auditorium during the town hall: the stage screen tiled with thirty live offices and a LIVE light; Noor with the runbook binder, Pim on the phone to APAC, Galen explaining something with open hands.
narration: This boss is different. First you decide the year — what the architecture gets. Then you mostly watch.
items.caption: Nobody here can reach Maya in less than ten minutes.

items.label: **☢ The Inheritance:** phase 1, the year — choose what the architecture gets. Phase 2, the town hall — watch what it does without you. Stepping in from the plane always works, and always costs.

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #121 · AVERY'S LENS  Design so the day goes right without you  The principal's test isn't whether you can save the day. It's whether what you built — the standard, the runbooks, the monitoring, the records and the people you trained — saves it while you're unreachable.  The biggest event of the year ran while its architect was over the ocean — and every save was made by someone else.

items.title: Nobody called.
items.body: Maya switches her phone on at the gate. No missed calls from the team. One message from Noor, sent at 14:41: ‘Town hall done. Five things went wrong. We held all five. Nothing needed you. — N.’ The log, when she reads it on the train, says the same in timestamps: an encoder failed and Pim was on the backup path in three minutes; monitoring heard an echo before any user did and Noor restored the template from DR-07; Galen turned down the CEO's office; captions were already in every room; Sabine found an expiring certificate in the records.
items.label: Test: the share held — and how much of the stream's allowance was used.

items.alt: A table of the town hall from 13:30 to 14:40: 13:35 primary encoder fails — Pim, RB-07, warm backup (E04); 13:45 EMEA template wiped — monitoring hears it, Noor restores DR-07 (E05, E06); 13:55 CEO's office wants firmware — Galen says not without a ticket (E03); 14:01 twenty-two rooms without captions — prevented, captions already everywhere (E09); 14:15 certificate expires — Sabine finds it in the records (E01, E05). Five of five held without Maya.
items.caption: Nothing needed her.

items.title: ‘Nothing needed you.’
items.body: Waiting on Maya's phone when she lands, sent at 14:41 headquarters time: ‘Town hall done. Five things went wrong. We held all five. Nothing needed you. — N.’

items.prompt: Friday, your last day. What happens to your access — and to your name?
known: ◉ Two items still with your name
items.risk: An architect who is still the system.
timeout: Maya's accounts are still active in March.

options.label: Keep your admin access for a month, just in case
options.fail: Access is security's, and it ends with the person.

options.label: Security disables every account of yours at 17:00 by their process; the last two items with only your name — a booking integration and a vendor contact — go to Pim and to a role in the records; your number comes out of every runbook; the team presents the town-hall log to Rashida, not you
options.result: Pim configures the integration while Maya watches in silence. At 17:00:00 Sabine's log shows every account disabled. Rashida: “Nothing needs you.”
options.consequence: Leaving is the last design step.

options.label: Hand your password-vault entries to Galen so nothing's lost
options.result: One single point of failure swapped for another.
options.consequence: Moves your keys instead of retiring them.
options.fail: Credentials are security's to retire, not the architect's to pass on.

options.label: Leave quietly — they know where to find you
options.result: They do. And for a year, they ring.
options.consequence: An architect who never quite left.

items.label: **Service Mode:** run the last day yourself.

items.alt: The architecture office at five on Friday; every dot on the estate board green; Noor, now the EMEA technician lead, grins; Maya with an empty lanyard in her hand.

bubbles.text: You didn't ring once. Were you worried?
Every minute. And I didn't ring, because you didn't need me to.

items.prompt: You didn't ring once. Were you worried?

options.label: “Every minute. And I didn't ring, because you didn't need me to — that was the whole year.”
options.reply: Then we'll keep not needing you. It's a compliment.

options.label: “I nearly messaged you about the template.”
options.reply: I had DR-07 open before you'd have finished typing.

items.alt: The architecture office the next Monday, without Maya: Rashida with the first lifecycle report of the new year; Galen; Pim briefing the week's rota.

bubbles.text: January's page is ready. Same three numbers.
Drill on Tuesday. Noor's running it.
APAC on-call: me, this week. Somebody else next week.

items.alt: The CityLight sanctuary, where it all began: the sound desk at the back, rows of empty chairs; Ray, older now, grinning; Maya holding a single sheet of paper — page one of a runbook.

bubbles.text: Heard you built something that doesn't need you.
That was the job. Now — who wants to learn the sound desk? I'll write it down so they won't need me either.

items.caption: Signal.

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  The principal's test is not whether you can save the day. It's whether what you built — standards with owned exceptions, a reserve the board sees, the right to stop, drilled runbooks that name roles, warm backups, monitoring aimed at people, decision records, access that works for everyone, and a team that can do every critical task twice over — saves it while you're out of reach. Stepping in always works for today and always costs tomorrow. Leaving is the last design step: your access ends on your last day, and nothing keeps only your name.
REFLECTION (optional)  · If you were over the ocean tomorrow, what would still work — and who would make it work?
